name: Science of Rules
title: A continuing inquiry into rules and regulation
tagline: Understanding how rules evolve, how regulation scales, and what AI changes.
intro: How do rules emerge, scale, and change—and when do they help complex systems adapt? Science of Rules brings together research on regulation across biological and social systems, the evolution of legal and organizational rules, and the effects of AI on institutional learning.
question: How do rules help complex systems grow and adapt?
question_text: From biological functions and organizations to laws and online communities, regulation makes collective activity possible. We study how its structure and costs change with scale, how rules persist or evolve, and whether institutions can keep learning as AI accelerates rule-making.
overview: Science of Rules is a growing home for research, people, and activities connected to the NSF Understanding the Rules of Life collaboration and the SNU Grand Quest project. We connect questions about the organization of complex systems with evidence on how rules evolve, and explore what AI changes about the creation, review, and revision of rules.

proposals.heading: Share a research proposal.
proposals.invitation: We welcome collaboration ideas, relevant datasets, methodological suggestions, and domain expertise on the evolution of rules and AI-assisted rulemaking.
proposals.prompt: Tell us about your idea, how it connects to this project, and the collaboration you have in mind.
